final_proposal.summary: The question 'number of female employees' matches employee-style tables with gender fields in at least two unrelated catalogs (human_resources.employee and works_cycles.Employee), and the pool also contains many employee-named tables lacking gender data. cases.question: Which crytocurrency had a bigger number of coins circulating in the market and in the general public's hands on 2013/4/28, Bitcoin or Litecoin?

final_proposal.summary: The coinmarketcap coins table (name) and historical table (coin_id, date, circulating_supply) appear sufficient to compare Bitcoin and Litecoin on 2013-04-28. However, the coins-to-historical join is not declared, so relationship metadata and human confirmation are needed before approval.

review.reviewer_notes_supervision_only: Required fields are coins.name, coins.id, historical.coin_id, historical.date and historical.circulating_supply. No declared relationship unit exists for coinmarketcap. The join coins.id=historical.coin_id is inferred from column names and descriptions only, so a relationship unit should be added. 'In the general public's hands' matches the circulating_supply description; total_supply is a weaker alternative reading. Name and date are ordinary filters and do not make table selection value-dependent. Only the review pool was inspected. No SQL was executed and no physical schema was verified.
